key.decision_why: The PR is still labeled "not ready" and the author made the fix Niloth-p asked for on CZO, so a triager needs to see it, but the approach and issue are unchanged, so a short note under the first card is enough.
key.action_why: On 2026-09-19 Niloth-p removed "not ready", added "maintainer review" and assigned herself and PieterCK, with no new request for work before that.
changed: Removed the six per-severity fixture files, so the PR went from +86/-5 in 8 files to +58/-5 in 2 files (view.py and tests.py), in line with Niloth-p's CZO guidance to loop over severity values on a single fixture.
On CZO the author said they set up Zabbix on a VM to capture a real payload, which answers the concern about LLM-generated fixtures.
On CZO the author named the PR they had studied (#37757), and Niloth-p redirected them to commit e4097a00 as the model to follow.
Tagged Niloth-p on GitHub for review, as she asked on CZO.
still_missing: The PR description and commit message still say the feature uses the opt-in `include_emoji_indicators` parameter, which the author says they removed on 2026-09-07.
There is no written answer on GitHub to Niloth-p's questions about which integrations or PRs were followed and what they did about doc.md.
The emoji mapping has no final approved plan linked from the PR, which issue #31240 asks for.
key.reply_ask: Thank the author, say the PR is moving to maintainer review with Niloth-p, and ask them to update the PR description and commit message to drop the stale `include_emoji_indicators` opt-in claim.

must_have.fact: Says the latest push removed the six per-severity fixture files (now +58/-5 in 2 files), which is the single-fixture approach Niloth-p asked for.
Notes that Niloth-p told the author on CZO to tag her on GitHub after updating, so this ping is the expected next step and not a premature one.
Recommends handing off: remove "not ready", add "maintainer review", and name Niloth-p as the reviewer (PieterCK is already the assignee).
Flags that the PR description still claims an `include_emoji_indicators` opt-in parameter that the author says was removed.
